meta.title: Someone Built a Country on an Abandoned Sea Fort
meta._convention: One scene-spec JSON per script, saved alongside it as <script-name>.scenes.json. Each beat's `duration` is intentionally omitted here -- build_video.js fills it in at render time from the ACTUAL measured length of that beat's generated narration WAV.
meta._note_not_a_country: Sealand is not a recognized sovereign state and has no polygon in world-atlas -- per README's 'Scenes that aren't a country' convention, highlight is left empty throughout and a gold marker + tiny hand-drawn platform outline at Roughs Tower's real coordinates (51.895 N, 1.4805 E, ~7nmi off the Suffolk/Essex coast) stands in for it.

beats.voText: In 1967, a man sailed out to an abandoned World War Two anti-aircraft platform in the North Sea, climbed aboard, and declared it a country.
It's called the Principality of Sealand, a concrete platform the size of two tennis courts, 7 miles off the English coast.
beats.onScreenText: The size of two tennis courts.

beats.voText: And it plays the part completely: Sealand has its own flag, its own currency, and its own passports, all issued from that one platform.
It even has a royal family. The Bates family has ruled Sealand for generations, surviving coup attempts, a fire, and decades on their own.
beats.onScreenText: A royal family. On a platform.

beats.voText: No country on Earth formally recognizes Sealand as a nation. But in nearly 60 years, no country has managed to shut it down either.
One abandoned fort, one declared nation, nearly 60 years of surviving on a concrete platform in the middle of the sea. Follow for more places on Earth that shouldn't exist, but do.
